problem.text: Ordinary MLP accepted activation_fn but ignored it: forward always applied SiLU.

reasoning.text: The constructor now resolves the activation once and forward invokes that callable between the up and down projections. Storing the callable and replacing the hard-coded call are dependent edits.

impact.text: The default remains SiLU; selecting "gelu" now requests PyTorch GELU with approximate="tanh". Projection construction and output-dtype conversion are unchanged.

The whole-parent-tree MLP search found no ordinary MLP construction sites or subclasses. Consequently, the demonstrated benefit is to the exposed module API, not an established existing model workflow.

source_notes.text: The preceding alignment entry records that activation_fn was newly accepted but unused. That entry was read; inspection of this patch shows its ignored-GELU observation is addressed.

Issue #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” concerns sliced GatedMLP loading and tensor-size mismatch. Its connection to this task is only an inferred shared-file relationship: the traceback names mlp.py, but this patch changes ordinary MLP activation, not sliced loading.

limitations: No PyTorch operation, model or GPU kernel was executed. PyTorch's implementation of the selected activations was not available in the inspected repository evidence; numerical accuracy and performance are unestablished.
No useful source-grounded numerical computation was needed for this callable-dispatch change; a scalar formula substitution would not test the selected PyTorch implementation.
Literal repository searches do not establish compatibility for dynamic or external callers.

claims.text: MLP now computes down(activation(up(x))) using a constructor-selected callable: F.silu for "silu", or a lambda invoking F.gelu with the tanh approximation for "gelu". This is selection at construction time, not a per-forward option; changing activation_fn alone afterward would not rebuild activation_fn_call.

The design resembles the existing GatedMLP selector but does not reuse its fused multiplication operations: ordinary MLP has one intermediate tensor, whereas GatedMLP passes gate and up tensors to ext.silu_mul or ext.gelu_mul. No existing F.gelu call was found in the parent tree.

TransformerBlock and ParallelDecoderBlock call their supplied mlp.forward without supplying an activation argument, so this patch does not require a forward-call signature change. Those consumers do not choose the new activation.

findings.description: Unrecognized activation strings leave the forward callable unset rather than producing an explicit configuration error.
findings.trigger: An external caller constructs an otherwise valid ordinary MLP with activation_fn="relu", then calls forward.
findings.expected_behavior: Reject the unsupported selection during construction or provide a defined activation.
findings.actual_behavior: Neither match arm assigns activation_fn_call; forward attempts to access it after the up projection. No in-tree ordinary MLP constructor caller was found, so reach is limited to the exposed API rather than a demonstrated model workflow.

verification.description: Compared the complete patch with the parent MLP implementation and searched the whole parent tree for MLP references; inspected transformer forward consumers.
verification.limits: No constructor or forward execution; external callers were not inspected.

annotation.summary: Makes ordinary MLP honor its activation selector, preserving SiLU by default and adding tanh-approximate GELU; unsupported strings remain unchecked.
